Hypothesis: We hypothesize that in patients with chronic liver disease, a comprehensive liquid biopsy panel that combines quantification of exosomal miRNAs (miR-21 and miR-221) with assessment of ctDNA methylation alterations (RASSF1A and GSTP1), supplemented by additional markers to adjust for inflammation and liver damage, will enable the early detection of aggressive hepatocellular carcinoma, including AFP-negative variants. This detection will be carried out using ultra-sensitive ddPCR and NGS techniques, with data consolidated and rigorously quality controlled through machine learning-driven bioinformatics pipelines. The novel integration of these molecular events—initiated by chronic liver injury and progressing through early HCC development, exosome secretion, and ctDNA alterations—culminates in a composite signature that can be identified prior to radiologic detection, thus allowing for earlier therapeutic intervention and improved patient outcomes.
Abstract: In patients with chronic liver disease, we propose a comprehensive, multi-omics liquid biopsy approach that integrates tumor-derived exosomal microRNAs (miR-21 and miR-221) with circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) methylation alterations in key tumor suppressor genes (RASSF1A and GSTP1) to facilitate the early detection of aggressive, including AFP-negative, hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Leveraging state-of-the-art digital droplet PCR (ddPCR) and next-generation sequencing (NGS) technologies for high-sensitivity quantification, the approach further employs advanced machine learning-based bioinformatics pipelines for robust data integration, normalization, and quality control. This refined strategy also incorporates additional inflammatory and liver-damage related molecular markers to control for potential confounders inherent in chronic liver pathology. As a result, the proposed composite biomarker signature is expected to be detectable before conventional radiologic changes occur, thereby providing a timely and non-invasive diagnostic tool for patient stratification and earlier intervention.
CausalChain: Chronic liver injury -> Early HCC development -> Secretion of tumor-derived exosomes (miR-21, miR-221) -> Aberrant ctDNA methylation (RASSF1A, GSTP1) -> Detection via ddPCR/NGS -> Machine learning integration and quality control -> Composite biomarker signature detectable pre-radiologically -> Identification of aggressive HCC features
